summary: whether a quantity changes along a sweep, by the exponent of a power law fitted to it and that exponent's standard error, against a tolerance and a multiple it is handed

inputs.name: sweep
inputs.meaning: the values the sweep took, all positive, in one unit

inputs.name: values
inputs.meaning: the quantity at each value of the sweep, all positive, in one unit

inputs.name: tolerance
inputs.meaning: the largest size of the exponent that counts as not changing; null when none is chosen

inputs.name: multiple
inputs.meaning: how many standard errors the exponent must clear the tolerance by, on either side; null when none is chosen

outputs.name: exponent
outputs.meaning: the least-squares slope of the logarithm of the values on the logarithm of the sweep; null below three points

outputs.name: exponent_standard_error
outputs.meaning: the slope's standard error, the residual sum over n - 2 over the sum of squared deviations, rooted; null below three points

validity: a quantity that goes as a power of the swept value over the sweep, with errors alike on every point; three points or more

source.citation: NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook of Statistical Methods, Section 4.4.3.1 Least Squares (read 2026-11-17, https://www.itl.nist.gov/div898/handbook/pmd/section4/pmd431.htm; meta_agent/inbox/materials/20261117-nist-sematech-least-squares); D. M. Lane et al., Online Statistics Education: A Multimedia Course of Study, Rice University, chapter Regression: Inferential Statistics for b and r; Standard Error of the Estimate (an open textbook) (read 2026-11-17, https://onlinestatbook.com/2/regression/inferential.html; meta_agent/inbox/materials/20261117-lane-online-statistics-regression)
source.locus: Sec. 4.4.3.1: the least-squares slope, the intercept and the residual standard deviation over n - p, p = 2 for a line; Inferential Statistics for b and r: s_b = s_est / sqrt(SSX); Standard Error of the Estimate: s_est = sqrt(sum (Y - Y')^2 / (N - 2))

note: v1 with its source changed from an encyclopedia page to a statistics handbook and a textbook, found by search; the code and the cases are v1's.
